## Problem and result
Implement physical sketch placement, snap and numeric input. Deliver the bounded result below within Alloy's standalone C++20 product; the current application is only a Qt shell.

## Scope
Add mouse placement and inline typed coordinates/lengths, documented snapping cues and explicit automatic-constraint policy for current line/rectangle tools. Complete the sourced Sketch Dimension flow: D, geometry selection, canvas annotation placement, numeric entry/Enter, repeated dimensions/Escape, and double-click annotation editing. Keep current palette coordinate helpers available while matching these reference interactions. Public sources and known gaps are in docs/research/commands/sketch-controls.md and sketch-reference-evidence.json.

Center-point rectangle placement and inline width/height Tab entry must have explicit coverage before TUT-002 can run.

## Acceptance criteria
- Physical placement dispatches the same authored commands; Escape/Enter/Tab and text focus work; inferred constraints are visible and removable.
- Dimension annotation placement and editing use shared observable command state; explicit conversion to driven is offered when a dependent driving dimension would overconstrain. Cancel and rejected solves preserve usable geometry and journal state.
- UI and local API share authoritative document/commands; expose arguments, selection, errors and result inspection. Undo/save coverage follows the dependencies, never a separate automation model.

## Proposed verification and evidence
Draw and dimension a rectangle with physical input, inspect its actual IDs/constraints through API and replay equivalent commands; capture cursor/constraint states separately.

Add/execute `python3 tests/workflows/run.py --case SKT-005 --evidence build/evidence/SKT-005` (case not implemented yet; the runner refuses missing cases). ## Problem and result
Add Join, Cut and Intersect directly to Extrude. Deliver the researched workflow through shared Alloy commands and authored history.

## Scope
Extend the existing profile extrusion command with explicit New Body, Join, Cut and Intersect operations and inspectable affected target-body selection. The generated prism is an ephemeral operation tool, not a separately authored tool-body feature. Support signed distance from origin or supported face sketches through the same document/session path.

## Acceptance criteria
Selecting a face sketch and Extrude Cut modifies the intended existing body in one feature and one undo entry. Join creates a boss on an existing body; Intersect retains overlap. Preserve target identity and source/profile dependency; recompute after upstream edits uses stored policy/IDs, never an invisible UI-only target list. Preview/cancel and invalid/no-overlap cases preserve live state.

## Proposed verification and evidence
Create a plate, sketch a radius-3 disk on its top face and cut 5 mm; inspect analytic removal45π, stable target identity and absence of a persistent cutter body. Join a rectangular boss and intersect a bounded volume. Inspect actual preview colors/result, explicit target list, native operation choice, undo/redo and reopen. SKT-017 joins this with face attachment/projection.

- Combine/Boolean research and dated public behavior are recorded externally, retrieved 2026-10-12.

## Limits and open questions
Keep Tools belongs to Combine and is not invented for the ephemeral extrusion tool. Symmetric/two-side, taper, through-all/to-object and thin-wall extent coverage remains SOL-010; declare any single-target/result limits.

## Problem and result
Attach sketches to planar faces with persistent references. Preserve the full roadmap while delivering a useful sketch-first increment.

## Scope
Extend origin-plane sketches to selected planar body faces, including faces produced by extrusion and non-axis-aligned planar faces. Support preselected face plus Create Sketch and command-first face selection. Retain a stable support reference and deterministic local frame evaluated before this sketch in feature history; changing face size must not recenter authored coordinates. Normal-to-plane entry is an explicit configurable behavior. Support outlines are not associative projected entities until SKT-010 implements them.

## Acceptance criteria
Create on the top face of an extrusion, then on an intact side face and an angled planar face through shared UI/API. Solved coordinates and extrusion normal map to the intended world plane. Supported upstream edits and reopen retain face identity and frame; deleted or ambiguous support produces an explicit repairable error without nearest-face fallback. Provide an explicit reselect/redefine-support path; never silently detach or move a sketch.

## Proposed verification and evidence
Create an extruded plate, select its top face, draw a second sketch and extrude it; repeat on a side and an inclined planar face. Change an upstream dimension and inspect world coordinates, support IDs and body geometry, then undo/reopen. Remove or ambiguously split support and verify atomic refusal or explicit unresolved/repair state. SKT-017 exercises the complete face/projection/dimension/cut chain. Separate native selection, API/geometry and actual visual evidence.

- Edit a sketch (reference `sketchmode`)
- Persistent geometry projection (reference `project`) — retrieved 2026-10-11. Reference descriptions are public evidence; fixture values and implementation boundaries are Alloy proposals.

## Limits and open questions
P0 next modeling sequence after the active circle/arc and Combine slices. Planar support is this scope; curved-surface wrapping/projection remains separate. Automatic edge projection is preference-sensitive and must not be claimed until linked entities and constraints exist.

## Problem and result
Project external geometry and repair lost projection links. Deliver the bounded result below within Alloy's standalone C++20 product; the current application is only a Qt shell.

## Scope
Project supported model edges and vertices into the active sketch with explicit associative-linked versus independent-copy choice. Store stable producer/edge/vertex provenance and resolve it at the sketch history position. Linked reference geometry is solver input, not editable duplicated coordinates; it can participate in dimensions, coincidence, parallelism and supported curve relations. Distinguish projected geometry visually. Creating a sketch on a planar face automatically exposes linked support-boundary references, following the current public Project documentation. Keep preference and explicit projection controls separately tracked; do not require an extra Project command for the tutorial Parallel-to-body-edge steps. Include relink, break-link and deletion repairs.

## Acceptance criteria
Projected lines, supported analytic curves and vertices preserve source identity through supported upstream edits. A dimension to a projected model edge recomputes the new sketch and downstream feature. A contextual body outline alone cannot satisfy this criterion. Missing/ambiguous/deleted source produces visible repair state or atomic rejection; no nearest-edge fallback, stale successful constraints or silent unlinking. Shared UI/API exposes source IDs, link status, errors and repair commands.

## Proposed verification and evidence
Project plate boundary edges into a face sketch; dimension a new point/circle from one edge using SKT-016 and add coincidence/parallelism where supported. Resize the plate so that referenced edge moves, then inspect the retained distance and changed world position/downstream geometry. Deliberately remove an edge and exercise relink, break and delete with undo/save/reopen. SKT-017 is the joined workflow gate; no API-only geometry substitutions.
